item.title: Wisconsin parent storms field during youth football game and trips 9-year-old kid in wild scene
item.description: A parent rushed the field during a U-10 football game in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, and tripped a 9-year-old heading for a touchdown during a live play.
item.content:encoded:
"Let the kids play" is something a lot of parents say when watching youth sports. However, one Wisconsin parent decided he wanted to become part of the action in a wild scene.

Last Saturday in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, a parent rushed the field during a U-10 football game and tripped a 9-year-old kid who was on his way to scoring a touchdown. The kid was running toward the pylon when the parent ran onto the field and stuck his leg out, taking out the runner.

The man who tripped the kid was found by Mount Pleasant police and was given a citation for disorderly conduct, according to FOX 6. He reportedly admitted he was wrong and was cooperative with authorities. The tripped player's coach, Channing Schultz, said the man intended to hurt the kid.

Schultz’s Case Eagles play the Milwaukee Colts again in two weeks, and he said the Colts have banned the parent from games. The tripper was the father of a kid on the opposing team.

item.title: Pennsylvania commissioner accuses Shapiro of 'deceptive' measles death framing as RFK Jr blasts Dem governor
item.description: Lancaster County Commissioner Joshua Parsons accuses Gov. Josh Shapiro of deception over measles-related deaths, saying the coroner has no record of them.
item.content:encoded:
A Pennsylvania county commissioner is challenging Gov. Josh Shapiro’s announcement of two measles-associated deaths, fueling a growing clash with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as the state’s outbreak swells to 460 confirmed cases across 31 counties.

Joshua Parsons, one of three Lancaster County commissioners, accused Shapiro of being intentionally "deceptive" during a press conference earlier this week, when the Democratic governor pointed to two "measles-related deaths" in the county.

"Well, the governor, in the press conference, they said they were measles-associated deaths, but it was framed, and very much the underlying assertion to it, was that these were measles deaths," Parsons told Fox News Digital.

During a Tuesday press conference alongside Dr. Debra Bogen at Penn Medicine Lancaster General Health Hospital, Shapiro announced the deaths of two people who were unvaccinated for measles.

"Today, we see the consequences of a lack of immunizations in the first measles-associated deaths that our Commonwealth has seen in 35 years," Shapiro said.

FORMER CDC ADVISER SAYS DECLINE IN KINDERGARTEN VACCINATIONS NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT: 'KEEP CALM AND CARRY ON'

Shapiro strongly urged Pennsylvanians to get vaccinated for measles during the press conference.

"I want to be clear: This illness and death from measles is completely preventable," he said.

Parsons said Shapiro cast the deaths as being the result of measles.

MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS

Parsons noted that national media outlets framed the deaths as being from measles. The New York Times, in a Tuesday story still posted to its website, wrote the headline, "Two Unvaccinated People Died From Measles in Pennsylvania, Officials Say."

MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS

However, according to conversations he had with the Lancaster County Coroner, Parsons claimed nobody in the county has died from measles this year.

"The coroner reported that they don't have… they had zero measles deaths or measles associated-deaths reported. And in Pennsylvania if you have someone who dies of a contagious disease, that does have to be reported to the county coroner," Parsons told Fox News Digital.

MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS

The coroner, Dr. Stephen Diamoantoni, has also publicly stated in interviews with local media that he had not been contacted by either Shapiro or the Pennsylvania Department of Health and was surprised to learn of the press conference.

"The coroner had one case where there was an infant who died in a home birth, and he's talked about this publicly, and that infant died with measles but not of measles. At the time of the press conference, the state did not indicate who these two cases were or anything about them. Subsequently, they came out and said that this infant is one of the ones they're counting," Parsons told Fox News Digital.

MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS

The Pennsylvania Department of Health, in a statement to Fox News Digital, asserted that it consistently referred to the cases as "measles-associated."

"PA DOH did not describe the cause of death of either individual. As PA DOH has repeatedly made clear since Tuesday, the Department consistently used the term ‘measles-associated’ in relation to these two deaths. That term means laboratory or epidemiologic evidence of measles is present — in both cases there was a positive measles test — but the disease may not be assessed by the medical certifier or coroner to be the immediate cause of death," the statement read.

MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS

The coroner did acknowledge the presence of measles in the infant who died, but said neither he nor the pathologist who examined the infant believed measles to be the cause of death.

The coroner, according to Parsons, said the infant died of a lacerated spleen. He also said he has received no information about the second person mentioned by Shapiro and the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS

Parsons said that suggested the deaths not being from measles.

"The Health Department put out a statement in reply to some of these questions. And I think it just raised more questions, but one line they had in there was that not all deaths in Pennsylvania have to be reported to the county coroner, and that's true. If you have, for example, an elderly person who dies of natural causes, that does not have to be investigated or reported to the coroner," Parsons said.

"But if you have someone who dies of an infectious disease, that does have to be reported. So if there is a second death in Lancaster County, that should have been reported," Parsons said. "Now, there's an unlikely scenario that someone contracted measles here and then died outside the county, and that would be reported to another county coroner. And if that's the case, which I think is highly unlikely, if it is the case, they should state that."

The Pennsylvania Department of Health, in response to Fox News Digital asking the department why it did not contact the coroner, said "Pennsylvania Statutes Title 16 (Pennsylvania Statutes Title 16 P.S. Counties § 4236 | FindLaw) outlines when a coroner would be called in to investigate a death. While DOH collaborates with county coroners in various ways, including death reporting, DOH does not regulate or oversee coroner operations, nor are coroners involved in most deaths within their county. "

Kennedy was also critical of Shapiro’s comments.

"Governor Shapiro's unseemly rush to Lancaster County to convene a national press conference and his giddy delight in announcing two measles deaths was a morose commentary on the contemporary political dialogue," Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. wrote in a Wednesday post on X.

"The performance was a replay of the Democrats' COVID playbook: fearmongering, misinformation, finger-pointing, and the weaponization of infectious disease fears for political gain," his post continued.

"The announcement appears to have been premature, and the deaths may even have been altogether fabricated by one of the Governor's hopeful staffers. The Lancaster County Coroner says that it has no record of any measles deaths. State law requires that all measles deaths be reported to the coroner," Kennedy also added.

Kennedy and Shapiro, according to The Washington Post, had a heated phone call just minutes before Shapiro’s Tuesday announcement. During the call, Shapiro reportedly told Kennedy he did not want the federal government’s help with the ongoing measles outbreak.

As of Friday, the Pennsylvania Department of Health said 460 measles cases have been confirmed across 31 counties in the state so far in 2026. It marks the nation’s largest measles outbreak since 1991, according to data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The majority of infected persons in the state are not vaccinated, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

Parsons highlighted that much of the outbreak is relegated to religious communities whose members choose not to get vaccinated.

"There's certainly measles here," Parsons told Fox News Digital. "There are in other Pennsylvania counties as well. And a lot of the focus has been on the plain population, Amish and Mennonites. Many of them choose not to get vaccinated. And by and large, they're going about their life and they're living their life and just continue on. So, we certainly have resources available for people if they wanna get vaccinated, but I believe strongly that's each individual's choice," Parsons concluded.

In response to a request for comment, Shapiro’s office referred Fox News Digital to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

Reached by Fox News Digital, a representative from the Times said the newspaper is "confident in the accuracy of our story."

Fox News Digital also contacted the White House and the Department of Health and Human Services for additional comment.

item.title: Men are skipping showers before dates for a reason that may surprise women
item.description: Pheromone-maxxing has men skipping showers and deodorant before dates, but the science behind natural body odor and attraction remains inconclusive.
item.content:encoded:
As if dating weren’t already enough of a gamble, a new trend has some men skipping their usual hygiene routines before meeting a prospective partner.

So-called "pheromone-maxxing" is a viral TikTok trend primarily associated with teen boys and young men that involves skipping showers and deodorant before a date. Some proponents go so far as to wear unwashed shirts or drink their own urine in an effort to "sweat out toxins," VICE reported.

'LOOKSMAXXING' TREND HAS YOUNG MEN TAKING HAMMERS TO THEIR FACES IN PURSUIT OF SHARPER FEATURES

Pheromones are chemical compounds that transmit signals between members of the same species. They are well documented in insects and other animals, and some pheromones do not have a discernible scent, Scientific American explained.

The theory behind pheromone-maxxing is that the stronger a man’s natural musk, the more sexually attractive he is.

The scientific evidence behind that idea, however, is inconclusive.

Researchers have found evidence that human body odors and secretions can influence physiological or psychological responses in other people.

"But there is no evidence of a consistent and strong behavioral response to any human-produced chemical cue," Scientific American reported. "To date, scientists have collected evidence for possible pheromone effects but have not definitively identified a single human pheromone."

One of the best-known experiments examining scent and attraction was a 1995 study commonly called the "sweaty t-shirt study."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Male participants wore the same T-shirt for two consecutive nights, after which female participants were asked to rate the odors of six shirts.

Women generally rated the body odors of men whose MHC (major histocompatibility complex) genes differed from their own as more pleasant than those of men with more similar MHC genes. The MHC is a group of genes that plays a key role in the immune system and may also influence individual body odor.

Among women taking oral contraceptives, however, that preference was reversed.

Later research has produced mixed results.

A 2019 study of 883 couples found that people from the Netherlands and Northern Europe were more likely to choose partners with different MHC genes. Researchers did not find the same pattern among Israeli couples and suggested a history of arranged marriages in some groups could help explain why.

A 2020 analysis of previous studies, however, found no strong evidence that people prefer partners with different MHC genes or find their body odor more attractive.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Pheromone-maxxing is tied to the broader "looksmaxxing" movement, in which social-media users attempt to optimize their appearance and attractiveness, sometimes through extreme measures such as cosmetic procedures and drastic diets.

Pheromone-maxxing has been making recent headlines, but the concept has circulated online since at least 2024.

A thread that year in the r/TikTokCringe subreddit drew a largely repulsed response.

"And how are those natural pheromones helping him in real life human social interactions?" one Redditor wondered.

"I am confused," commented another. "Does he think that bathing means you no longer make pheromones? Is nobody able to teach him?"

"There’s no way in hell I would let my child go to school or even in my house smelling stinky," another user wrote. "It’s actually sad that no one in his life has taught him the importance of cleanliness."

Discussing the trend on Fox News’ "The Five," co-host Jesse Watters said, "I’m anti-cologne."

He recommended a simple pre-date shower with bar soap and shampoo.

Panelist Tyrus agreed and urged men to use unscented deodorant.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"If men put too much cologne on, you’re a creep," he said. "You’re sending the wrong message. You don’t want to smell like gym class, but you also don’t want to smell like you’re cheap."

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Woke Virginia tears down statue of Geneva Convention pioneer
item.description: Hunter Holmes McGuire's statue was removed from Richmond capitol grounds despite his role in creating the Winchester Accord.
item.content:encoded:
Do not adjust your calendars. You may have seen images this week of Confederate statues coming down in Richmond’s capitol grounds, and thought we had slipped back in time to the tumult of 2020, but no. Rather, the commie Commonwealth of Virginia is still tearing down American history in the year of our Lord 2026.

As bad as the removal of all of these monuments has been, this particular round of damnatio memoriae on Friday, captured in its illiberal net the statue of a man named Dr. Hunter Holmes McGuire, whose work provided a major contribution to the Geneva Convention, the global gold standard of wartime humanitarian rules.

McGuire served as a Confederate surgeon for almost the entirety of the Civil War, saving countless lives. One life he failed to save was that of General Thomas "Stonewall" Jackson, who died under the doctor’s care. A Jackson statue also came down on Friday.

GENDER EQUITY, DEI, CLIMATE ACTION: HOW THE SMITHSONIAN'S WOKE PUSH 'INFILTRATED' AMERICA'S MOST BELOVED ZOO

Once again, the good Dr. McGuire could not save Stonewall.

It was under Jackson’s command in 1862 that McGuire established a new humanitarian principle of warfare that we still have with us today, not just in the United States, but across the world.

In May 1862, after the First Battle of Winchester, 6 Union army doctors were captured. It was then that McGuire convinced a reluctant Jackson to release them, and established, with Northern agreement, the Winchester Accord, after which both sides released doctors as non-combatants.

McGuire himself would be released by the North under the accord in 1864, and would go on to be present for the Confederate surrender at Appomattox Courthouse.

The Winchester Accord would be adopted by the Geneva Convention, offering protection to medical personnel in wars that they still enjoy today, and yet, despite all of this, his statue was toppled, just like all the others.

As usual, the destroyers of monuments brook no nuance in their march to destroy American history. If you wore the wrong uniform, your statue has to go and you have to be disgraced.

According to Democratic state Senator Mike Jones, McGuire’s statue had to be removed because, "I remembered seeing white only, colored only pictures in my mother’s scrapbook, and so to have that as a visual and then for these things to remain to remind this area of what took place, I think it’s wrong."

I’m sorry, but the fact that Jones is made uneasy by metal statues because they remind him of racism that occurred 70 years ago is the kind of silly claptrap that should have been left in the madness of 2020, and yet here we are.

Allow me to go a bit further and argue that if you took the accomplishments of every person involved with having McGuire’s statue removed, they would not begin to equal his contributions to the humanization of modern military conflict.

It really is incredible. Day and night, night and day, the progressive left goes on and on about alleged war crimes committed by Israel, or the United States, and yet in their ignorance and simple-mindedness they are defaming a man who played a key role in creating the definitions of those very alleged crimes.

TRUMP V. SMITHSONIAN: A TIMELINE OF HOW THE WHITE HOUSE FIGHT OVER 'WOKE' HISTORY UNFOLDED

The same people who freak out with hair afire when the Trump administration tries to make the Smithsonian museums just a skosh more patriotic, are perfectly happy tearing down a statue of a man whose work saved thousands, maybe millions of lives.

Democrats will insist that unlike in 2020, when mobs just tore statues down willy-nilly, this decision went through a process run by democratically elected officials, and sure. But we all know that there is never a conservative on the blue ribbon panels they create to destroy Southern heritage.

The very slight silver lining in all of this is that McGuire’s statue, as well as the other two removed on Friday, will be moved to battlefield sites by the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields Foundation.

A spokesperson for that vital organization said, "Preservation is more about the future than the past … At the core of all we do is the belief that our shared history can unite the people of our nation; that there is strength and inspiration for our own times to be found in the struggles of the past."

Hear Hear.

But those statues belong where they were, in the place of honor the capitol originally provided.

Make no mistake, reports of the demise of Woke 1.0 aren’t just exaggerated, they are nonsense, as Friday’s statue removals prove, and our fight against this anti-historical intolerance must not wane, but rather grow in its strength and dedication.

item.title: Triathlete who survived alligator attack tells harrowing story of his escape: 'I got super lucky'
item.description: Jonathan Bruney reveals how squeezing an alligator's eye saved his arm during a Savannah River training swim near Augusta for an Ironman competition.
item.content:encoded:
A triathlete who survived an alligator attack in the Savannah River shared his story with OutKick OutDoors.

Jonathan Bruney took a trip to the Georgia/ South Carolina border for what he thought would be a routine day of training for an upcoming Ironman competition.

"This was a work trip for me as a coach to bring my athletes down to the river on a recon course day, is what we call it," Bruney explained.

BOATER SCARED OFF ALLIGATOR, THEN USED ROPE TO STOP BLEEDING AFTER FLORIDA WOMAN LOST ARM

"We all went down to Augusta, we got ready to swim, and this was just going to be a nice, easy zone-two, low-heart-rate day. Just going through each portion of the course."

While he was leading the pack, Bruney felt a bump on his elbow that turned the whole day into a fight for survival.

FLORIDA MAN GIVES AN INCREDIBLE INTERVIEW ABOUT HOW HE FOUGHT OFF AN ALLIGATOR WITH A FISHING POLE

"I was breathing and sighting on my left side … and he was on my right. That’s when my elbow felt the brute of the force."

Bruney thought the alligator, which he described to be anywhere between five and six feet, was a log.

"I wasn’t even thinking gator," said Bruney. "I’m thinking, ‘Okay, big log floating in the river.’ But then I looked to my right. I’m like, ‘Okay, this is a lot worse than a log.’"

Almost immediately, Bruney's fight or flight instincts kicked into overdrive.

FLORIDA WILDLIFE OFFICIALS CONFIRM 13-FOOT GATOR KILLED ORLANDO WOMAN WITH 'DEATH ROLL' ON RIVER

"This thing’s big enough to barrel roll and rip the arm off if I don’t get away quickly," he recalls.

His next move may have ultimately saved his life, or at the very least, his arm.

"I did have two moderate punches, but that didn’t do anything… [I] went up the snout and squeezed the eye."

Bruney explains that he learned about the eyes being sensitive spots from watching "Shark Week" (who says you can't learn anything from TV shows).

After making it to shore, Bruney wasn't just worried about his own safety, but for the safety of his fellow athletes, too.

"I hope this gator doesn’t bite one of my athletes," he said.

None of the swimmers had their phones on them, so a good samaritan had to dial 9-1-1.

While that was taking place, a friend of Bruney's was able to stop the bleeding using a cord from his swim buoy.

NEARLY 2,000 OCEAN RESCUES OCCUR AS DANGEROUS SURF SLAMS POPULAR BEACHES THIS SUMMER

By the time the first responders arrived, Bruney was starting to feel dizzy and his entire arm was running cold.

He credits the police officers and EMTs, who were first to arrive on the scene, with keeping him calm and treating his wounds.

"The police officers, they came on scene pretty quickly. I mean, within a few minutes I heard their sirens," Bruney said. "They actually wrapped my arm up. Pretty good props to them for knowing what to do. And then the ambulance came."

While the doctors cleared him to continue training for his competition, Bruney admits there was a moment of doubt.

But after giving it some thought, he said there was no way he was going to let this deter him.

"Being able to remove my race entry, that’s not on the books. I can’t do that."

When I asked him whether he would ever go back in the water, Bruney didn't hesitate.

"We’ll be back in there," he said, confidently.

item.title: Star student rejected by 16 colleges, hired by Google, gets legal win in racial discrimination suit
item.description: A Palo Alto, California, father declares victory after a judge denied the University of Washington's motion to dismiss their anti-Asian bias suit.
item.content:encoded:
A father in Palo Alto, California is declaring a victory in court after a federal judge allowed a civil rights lawsuit alleging anti-Asian bias in college admissions to move forward.

Nan Zhong and his son, Stanley Zhong, filed federal lawsuits against several elite institutions — including the University of California system, the University of Washington, the University of Michigan, and Cornell University. The complaints allege the universities engaged in "racially discriminatory admissions practices that disadvantage highly qualified Asian-American applicants."

One of their cases will now proceed in part against the University of Washington after a federal judge granted the university defendants' motion to dismiss in part and denied it in part.

"We got an exciting ruling from the judge," Nan Zhong told Fox News Digital. "Effectively, the judge ruled in our favor by denying the university's motion to dismiss. So this is a major development in the lawsuit. That means the judge found enough factual allegations to support our allegation."

DUKE LAW'S ALLEGED RACE-BASED ADMISSIONS ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT RULING: DOJ

The ruling centered in part on sovereign immunity. Judge James L. Robart denied the defendants' motion to dismiss Stanley's Title VI claims against the university while dismissing several other claims.

The University of Washington Board of Regents sent Fox News Digital a statement in response to the ruling.

"We're pleased that the court dismissed many of the claims and two of the three plaintiffs. Admission to the Allen School is highly competitive and the vast majority of out-of-state applicants are not admitted because, as Washington’s flagship university, we prioritize Washington residents for admission," a spokesperson said.

"With that ruling, we can now proceed into discovery, request internal documents, internal communication, and most importantly, admissions data," Nan said.

Stanley Zhong, now 21, made headlines after he was rejected by 16 of the 18 colleges he applied to — including top-tier public and private institutions — despite boasting an elite academic record. A 2023 graduate of Gunn High School in Palo Alto, Stanley scored a 1590 out of 1600 on the SAT (99th percentile), held a 4.42 weighted GPA, ranked in the top 9% of his graduating class, and had launched a free e-signing startup featured by Amazon Web Services.

Shortly after the college rejections, Google hired Stanley as a full-time software engineer in a position that his family's court filing says typically requires a Ph.D. or equivalent practical experience. Stanley was first scouted by the tech giant in coding competitions when he was just 13 years old.

CALIFORNIA SOCIOLOGY PROFESSOR CITED 'IRONY' IN REMOVING ACT/SAT, NOT FIXING RACIAL DISPARITIES AS INTENDED

The family spent over a year researching admissions trends before filing the lawsuits, concluding that anti-Asian bias remains a systemic issue despite recent court precedents.

"The story is much bigger than myself, than my son, Stanley, or our family," Zhong told Fox News Digital. "First of all, I have a younger son, so I don't want him to face the same problem that his older brother faced. I think this is something important we should correct so my future grandkids won't have the same problem again."

Zhong added that since taking their battle public, dozens of families across the country have reached out to share similar experiences.

"After the story came out, we received a lot of communication from other Asian-American families telling us about their story, telling about how highly qualified Asian-American students were rejected left and right," Zhong said. "So this is a large-scale issue and I think of it as an issue that's been around for a long time."

CALIFORNIA BOARD OF REGENTS TO REVIEW SAT/ACT TESTING BAN AFTER 1,400 PROFESSORS WARN OF ‘SEVERE’ MATH GAPS

Spokespersons for the University of California system have previously denied the allegations, maintaining that their admissions policies strictly comply with state and federal laws prohibiting race-conscious decisions.

Stanley Zhong was accepted at the University of Maryland and the University of Texas-Austin but decided to take a job offer as a software development engineer at Google in the fall of 2023 instead.

item.title: Ex-Hillary Clinton staffer warns Democrats that courting far-left could cost them Jewish voters
item.description: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel accused Democratic leadership of pushing Jewish voters out and warned the party risks losing them over antisemitism.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel this week issued a blunt warning to Democratic leadership ahead of the upcoming midterms: Stop minimizing Jewish voters’ concerns, or they’ll walk. Former Hillary Clinton staffer Kaivan Shroff agreed, saying the issue is whether Jewish Democrats will feel like they have to "explain or defend a basic part of their identity to remain in good standing with the party."

Appearing on the Atlantic’s "David Frum Show," Nessel accused the Democratic Party of not valuing its Jewish constituents and making them feel less welcome than members of other minority groups.

"I think it’s a fundamental mistake for the Democratic Party to think that you can just push Jewish Democrats out and simply replace them with any other population," Nessel told Frum on Wednesday’s podcast episode.

DEMOCRATIC MICHIGAN AG ACCUSES HER PARTY OF 'ABSOLUTELY NOT' DOING ENOUGH TO COUNTER ANTISEMITISM

Nessel's comments were echoed by Shroff, a media commentator and former digital organizer for Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign. Shroff told Fox News Digital that Democrats risk losing key Jewish voters as the party grapples with internal divisions over its ideological direction.

"What Nessel is saying should make Democrats nervous because this isn’t really a debate about Netanyahu or even Israeli policy — it’s about whether Jewish Democrats are starting to feel like they have to explain or defend a basic part of their identity to remain in good standing with the party," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "Ironically, Democrats cannot afford to keep shrinking their political tent in the name of expanding it to folks like Hasan Piker — and then act surprised when pieces of the coalition start walking out."

Shroff added that Democratic leaders should stop courting socialist-aligned candidates and start shoring up the establishment supporters who have long defended the party — especially ahead of the midterm elections.

"Of course, Nessel is a prominent Democrat in Michigan — a state where a lot of this debate has now centered around Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and his affiliation with streamer Hasan Piker, who has made controversial comments that many other Democrats have just condemned as antisemitic," Shroff said. "It’s a critical Senate seat for Democrats to win and they need all their voters and more to show up. So turning off loyal Democrats like Nessel is a huge issue and should be causing major alarm."

MICHIGAN'S DEMOCRATIC AG REFUSES TO ATTEND UPCOMING CONVENTION OVER HARASSMENT CONCERNS

According to Nessel, Jewish Democrats have felt ostracized by their own party following the attacks in Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, and accused leadership of cherry-picking issues that are relevant to supporters.

"When a Black person says that a phrase that you’re using or the way you’re talking about this issue to me is racist, I’d like you to stop doing it — we respect that," Nessel said on The David Frum podcast. 

JEWISH HOUSE DEMOCRAT RECALLS COLLEAGUE SAYING THERE IS NO ANTISEMITISM BECAUSE 'ALL THE JEWS ARE RICH'

Nessel then pointed to what she said was a discrepancy in how members of her party handle concerns raised by Jewish voters.

"This has been an outlier to me," Nessel said. "I have people saying, ‘You are not going to tell us what you deem to be antisemitic. We’ll decide what’s antisemitic. That’s not up for you, the Jewish population, to decide.’"

"I find that to be very off-putting and offensive," she continued. "I think that’s totally unacceptable."

BATYA UNGAR-SARGON EXPLAINS WHY SO MANY AMERICAN JEWS BECAME DEMS — AND WHY SOME NOW FEEL POLITICALLY HOMELESS

Following her condemnation of the Democrats’ treatment of Jewish constituents’ concerns regarding antisemitism, Nessel added that if faced with the choice, she would choose her Jewish heritage over her party affiliation.

"If that’s the deal that has to be made, and I’ve been really candid about this, I was Jewish before I was ever Michigan attorney general — I’m going to be Jewish afterwards," Nessel said.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRATIC SENATE CANDIDATE CLAIMS ISRAEL 'JUST AS EVIL' AS HAMAS

"I was Jewish before I was ever a member of the Democratic Party, and if I have to, I’ll be Jewish afterwards too," she continued.

Nessel also took aim at Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, for previous comments he made following an attempted terrorist attack on a synagogue in West Bloomfield earlier this year, in which he remarked, "Hurt people do hurt people."

MICHIGAN SENATE RACE: EL-SAYED’S TIES TO EXTREMIST FUEL ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS AMONG JEWISH VOTERS

"A lot of us perceived that as sort of making excuses for someone that sought to murder over 100 pre-K schoolchildren and that’s the kind of mentality that bothers me a lot," Nessel said.

She added that although El-Sayed has met with Jewish leaders in the community, his unwillingness to retract his previous comments is cause for concern and risks amplifying such views.

Nessel did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment. Fox News Digital also reached out to the El-Sayed campaign for comment. 

Piker previously told his viewers, "If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews."

Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who is Jewish, called out Piker this week in response. In a social media post. She wrote, "This shouldn’t be hard: no community should face the threat [of] violence for their political views. Period," 

Slotkin continued, "That goes if you’re pro-Israel, pro-Palestine, pro-choice, pro-life or any other cause you care about. And blaming the victims of violence for bringing it on themselves only further endangers people."

item.title: From spit on to hugged, Riley Gaines unlocks main problem with the WNBA, and it’s as simple as red vs blue
item.description: Riley Gaines received hugs and smiles at an Indiana Fever game after being booed in Minneapolis, highlighting the red state-blue state divide in the WNBA.
item.content:encoded:
What a difference a red state makes.

Unapologetic and steadfast, Riley Gaines, the nation’s leading advocate for the preservation of women’s sports for biological women, gets under the skin of woke leftists without even trying.

She travels the country, and says that biological men don’t belong. The audacity!

THESE FEMALE ATHLETES NEED TO SPEAK UP ABOUT KEEPING WOMEN'S SPORTS FOR WOMEN, LIKE SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DID

In some places in this country, Gaines gets booed for speaking this simple logic and truth. She gets yelled at. Even spit on for her beliefs.

That was the kind of reception Gaines got at her very first WNBA game in Minneapolis earlier this summer, when she dared to take a sign into the arena that praised Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham for bravely speaking up for girls in girls' sports.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS RALLY IN INDIANA WHILE DISPLAYING WHAT MAKES AMERICA GREAT

Fast-forward to her second-ever WNBA game, Friday night in Indianapolis at an Indiana Fever game in which former NBA player Royce White (now sometimes going by "Roysha") made a surprise appearance, and Gaines got a much different reception.

Hugs, smiles, requests for photographs.

ROYCE WHITE SHOWS UP TO INDIANA FEVER GAME IN BLONDE WIG AMID WNBA DRAFT PURSUIT

Blue state, red state. Delusional, sensible. Hostile, friendly.

Perhaps this is part of the problem with the powder keg that is the WNBA. There are 15 teams in the league, and only two are located in solid red states: the Indiana Fever and the Dallas Wings. Atlanta, Las Vegas and Phoenix have teams, but those states aren’t reliably red, more purple. The league is adding Cleveland in 2028, so that might help, but the scale will still be far from balanced.

"My main takeaway is that when Minneapolis is booing you, it’s generally a good sign," Gaines told OutKick with a bit of tongue-in-cheek during halftime of Friday’s game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, which the Fever won easily over the Connecticut Sun, 111-91. "Especially for those of us with common sense and an ounce of integrity and a shred of honesty."

If there were people in the Fever crowd on Friday that were more Minneapolis than Indianapolis, you wouldn’t know it. Just a different atmosphere and decorum altogether. And that fuels Gaines.

The poor reception in Minneapolis didn’t deter her at all. Knowing that so many people across the United States agree with her does.

On Friday, as she supported Cunningham and White, Gaines proudly sported a black T-shirt with neon green XX-XY lettering, a label so controversial in some (blue!) WNBA cities that fans at an Atlanta Dream game were recently asked to cover that same shirt.

STEPHANIE WHITE, LET ME 'EDUCATE' YOU ON THE SCIENCE OF WHY MEN DON'T BELONG IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

The nonsense on gender in the WNBA is incessant. And neither White nor Enes Kanter Freedom could stand to sit back and watch it a second longer.

Earlier this month, White joined Freedom, another former NBA star, in saying that they now identify as trans women while also declaring their interest in joining the WNBA next year via the 2027 WNBA Draft.

Freedom and White decided to fight lunacy with lunacy, using their over-the-top declarations as a way to push back on the WNBA’s lack of spine and clarity in the trans in women’s sports dilemma.

If the WNBA can’t define a woman, can’t put clear language into its bylaws that limits participation in the league to strictly biological women, then Freedom and White say that they will take this fight as far as they can. They say that trying to play in the WNBA isn’t talk, that they are prepared to walk that walk if necessary. They are also prepared to fight through litigation if necessary.

While Freedom was ejected from a WNBA game he attended last week in blue Chicago (Sky player Natasha Cloud sniped at him during the game, he responded, fans booed him, and he was ultimately permanently banned from Wintrust Arena), White was received warmly in red Indiana.

No boos. No yelling. Instead, fans approached White with smiles and respect and outstretched arms for handshakes and fist bumps. They asked for photos. They thanked him, told him they loved what he is doing for women's sports.

"You can't expect that, it was overwhelming," White told OutKick, regarding his Indiana welcome. "But...I think people have a lot of appreciation for what Roysha is doing and some of the other people who are fighting as well. It's just so crazy to me the difference in response here in Indiana versus in Chicago (for Freedom). But one city is run by people who have common sense and the other one isn't, so there's that."

Gaines received similar treatment at Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

"Let me tell you the difference, being here in Indiana, a home game for the Fever," Gaines said. "The looks that you’re getting are smiles, people are winking. People are coming up and saying thank you. People are expressing their gratitude for the stance that I (have taken).

"Not the same response I had in Minneapolis."

Gaines expects nothing less from blue cities and blue states now. She understands her messaging in those areas requires her to bring a much stiffer upper lip, and an extra layer of Teflon coating.

And even though that's expected, it's not always easy, which is why she so deeply respects and appreciates what Freedom and White are doing. Gaines and White talked at length at halftime of Friday’s game about their convictions on the trans in women’s sports dilemma.

Gaines said that it is ironic that WNBA players like Cloud from the Chicago Sky are missing the point of what Freedom and White are trying to do.

"I was watching the altercation between Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha (Cloud) where obscenities were yelled back and forth, at least on Natasha’s end at Enes, and I thought to myself, ultimately, Natasha really should be thanking Enes, because what he’s fighting for…is her," Gaines said. "He is fighting for her to have the opportunity and the ability to achieve and to exceed in her sport and even beyond."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Others besides White and Freedom are fighting alongside Gaines for the very same thing.

The Indiana Attorney General, Todd Rokita, who sat with Gaines and her husband during Friday's game, has been active in trying to protect girls and women in sports.

"I’m pleased to host my friend Riley Gaines tonight with her husband and we’re having a good time," Rokita told OutKick. "But the fact of the matter is, there are a lot of leaders in this country who see the obvious, and the obvious is that sports teams should only have the same biological sex because there are differences. And I am so happy that these biological men (Freedom and White) are proving the point when they are coming to apply for the WNBA solely because the WNBA can’t get its own bylaws straight."

What is happening in the WNBA, with the ambiguity surrounding eligibility, concerns Rokita because it could just as easily happen elsewhere, which creates a slippery slope.

"As Indiana’s Attorney General, I am looking at this very closely, from the perspective of whether you are for-profit or non-profit, the fact that you have bylaws that make sense and comply with all laws and that they are clear and non-abusive," Rokita said. "And if you can’t define in your bylaws what a woman is and who’s eligible to be on your teams, you’re entering a real gray area in terms of law, in terms of being abusive or deceptive to those you serve.

"If the WNBA can’t make some simple decisions about what their bylaws should read, you may see a lot of states, a lot of my friends, get involved, including Indiana."

Now wouldn’t that be something? How ironic if it is a couple of men pretending to be women, along with red-state fans and politicians, who ultimately save the very woke and leftist and blue WNBA from itself. It really could be as simple as that.

Does the WNBA need more red-state teams? Let me know at: patricia.babcockmcgraw@outkick.com

item.title: Byron Donalds shuts down Bill Maher’s claim on GOP primary racism, says 'Florida is a meritocracy'
item.description: Byron Donalds pushed back on Bill Maher's claims that racism cost him key Florida Panhandle counties, calling the state a meritocracy on "Real Time."
item.content:encoded:
Florida gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds rejected comedian Bill Maher’s claims that he lost key counties in the recent primary in part due to the racism within the state.

Appearing on HBO's "Real Time with Bill Maher" Friday night, Donalds, the Republican gubernatorial nominee, pushed back on host Bill Maher's assertion that he lost parts of Florida's Panhandle because of the area's predominantly White electorate.

"You did lose the ‘Redneck Riviera’ badly," Maher said, referring to Donalds’ losses in Calhoun, Columbia, Dixie, Gilchrist, Hamilton, Hardee, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Levy, Liberty, Madison, Suwannee, Taylor, Union, and Washington counties — rural counties where roughly 94% of Republican voters are White.

STEPHEN A SMITH ADMITS BYRON DONALDS COULD MAKE HIM A REPUBLICAN, CALLS HIM ‘THE REAL DEAL’

"I can’t get with you on a lot of this policy stuff," Maher continued. "But I think it would be great if the country did have [its] first Black, Republican governor."

Maher went on to praise Donalds for his willingness to run in "this post-racial world" where constituents don’t care about the "color of their skin," but he added that "we’re not quite there yet though."

BILL MAHER BLASTS CALIFORNIA'S EDUCATION RESULTS, CITES TWO SURGING RED STATES

"The Redneck Riviera, which is the Panhandle," Maher began. "I think there are people there who still would not — you’re a Republican, you’re a Trumper — they should love you and they don’t. I think there is still racism."

"Let’s talk a little bit about the Panhandle," Donalds replied, beginning his rebuttal. "There are counties we did incredibly well in that we won. There were some counties that we fell a little short in, that’s okay."

WATCH: BYRON DONALDS BRUSHES OFF GOP DEBATE DEMANDS AS RIVALS LAG FAR BEHIND IN POLLS

Donalds then pointed out the crowded Florida primary field which had 11 Republicans on the ballot, with candidates "who had various lines of support."

"The number one thing overall, we closed out 48% of the vote in Florida," Donalds said. "800,000 votes [is] a long way to becoming the nominee."

TRUMP-BACKED NOMINEES DOMINATE PRIMARY CONTESTS AS PRESIDENT TIGHTENS PARTY VICE GRIP

Donalds went on to push back against Maher's argument that racial bias influenced the primary results, insisting that Florida is a place where people can pursue opportunities in elected office.

"Florida really has become the microcosm of what we all want," Donalds said. "It's a meritocracy. And it's about the best person with the best views, the best skills, the best talent moving forward to represent your state or to represent a district in your state, and Florida exemplifies that."

GIANNO CALDWELL: FLORIDA NEEDS BYRON DONALDS TO PROTECT THE DESANTIS LEGACY

However, former Florida state Sen. Dave Aronberg was not as quick to attribute Donalds' showing to the crowded primary field.

"When you look at the primary numbers, Byron Donalds falling short of 50% does raise some legitimate questions," Aronberg told Fox News Digital. "Yes, there were 11 names on the ballot, but few of his opponents were viable contenders, and Donalds had a massive fundraising and name recognition advantage compared to the rest of the field. It wasn't exactly a neck-and-neck dogfight."

FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: DEMOCRATS LEAD IN THE HOUSE, BUT REDISTRICTING KEEPS THE GOP IN THE GAME

Aronberg added, "When you see him underperforming in certain rural pockets, it's hard to completely dismiss race having played at least some quiet role." "Going into November, Republicans have a massive advantage in party registration and financial resources. But this will be no cakewalk based on what we saw in the primary, along with President Trump’s lagging poll numbers and the quality of his Democratic opponent."

‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES

Maher later challenged Donalds on his campaign platform by pointing to President Donald Trump’s tariffs impacting affordability across the country — especially in Florida.

"I don't feel like the president's policies are making that affordable part easy for you," Maher said.

A POPULAR COCKTAIL HAS A TRUMP TRADE PROBLEM YOU PROBABLY DIDN’T KNOW ABOUT

"Even the Wall Street Journal, which is usually pretty far right, calls this trade war with Canada the ‘dumbest trade war,’ that's the title," Maher continued. "It says Republicans are already getting pounded on the campaign trail over his tariffs and inflation, mostly because of the war. Byron, are you getting pounded on the campaign trail?"

"I think that people in Florida are thinking about their pocketbooks. Well, that's like anywhere else," Donalds said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

He went on to defend Trump’s tariffs on Canada, adding that the president is reevaluating trade policies that are not working for the American people.

"But I would rather have a chief executive that looks at these deals and engages these other countries and fights for Americans, [rather] than just lets them roll knowing that they're not gonna be in the interest of small businesses," Donalds said.

item.title: College football Week 0 betting picks for North Carolina v. TCU and San Jose State vs USC
item.description: College football Week 0 kicks off with North Carolina vs. TCU and San Jose State vs. USC, featuring Bill Belichick's Tar Heels and key betting picks.
item.content:encoded:
Can you believe we are already there? We've reached that point in the year when we have football once again. Looking at the calendar, it is wild to me that we are almost at the end of August. Time really does fly when you're having fun.

It has been a good year for sports betting, and it is now getting even better as we have Week 0 starting today with college football returning. College Football is back, and so is our betting slate. Let's get to it.

Both of these teams started last year against each other, and I have to imagine both are looking for better outcomes than their 2025 campaign. North Carolina was rocked in head coach Bill Belichick's first game at the helm. They looked lost on both offense and defense and fell 48-14.

The rest of the campaign wasn't much better as the team had a 4-8 record overall. Looking at their wins, there really weren't any that were overly impressive, either. The Tar Heels hope to be better this year, but this is a long rebuilding process. You can't expect it to happen overnight.

BILL BELICHICK ANNOUNCES SON STEVE IS ON MEDICAL LEAVE FROM NORTH CAROLINA FOOTBALL PROGRAM

After the win to open the season last year, TCU took down Abilene Christian and SMU. From there they lost on the road to Arizona State and Kansas State. After beating Baylor and West Virginia, the team lost to Iowa State and BYU in back-to-back weeks. They did beat Houston, a ranked team, later in the season. They also had one of the better Bowl Games to watch as they won over USC in overtime, 30-27.

The reason for optimism this season is around Jaden Craig taking over under center. He comes over from Harvard, where he was successful, but the team wasn't very good. Jeremy Payne will be the featured back and could make this a dangerous backfield after a strong 2025.

I like the chances of seeing some good offense from TCU. I don't love the total for the game, as I think it probably goes under 46.5, but we've already lost three points from the opening number. I am instead just focused on the TCU team total. I'll back them to go over 27.5 points. I think they should get a touchdown in each quarter as I still think this North Carolina defense will struggle.

There aren't a ton of lopsided games on the slate for today, but this is certainly one of them. San Jose State is expected to be blown out to start the year. USC has manhandled the Spartans in the past, having crushed them in their past three matches. Collectively, USC has won the last three matchups by a score of 146-38. Last year was an ugly season for the Spartans as they finished 3-9, missing out on any Bowl Game. They also went just 2-6 in the Mountain West.

THREE TEAMS RANKED OUTSIDE THE TOP-12 OF THE COACHES POLL WHO WILL MAKE THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

USC has a chance to march to its first College Football Playoff berth, but it won't be the easiest path.

They enter the season ranked at number 14 in the nation. That puts them right on the borderline of making the postseason tournament. Either way, they should be able to get a great Bowl Game even if they don't get into the playoffs.

They have some important continuity here as Jayden Maiava returns to action. Last season, Maiava had 3,711 yards and 24 touchdowns. King Miller returns to the backfield as well, and should lead the way for the squad. They did lose Makai Lemon to the NFL, so there are some questions about who steps up as a receiver.

The Trojans are listed at 50.5 for their team total, and I just think that's too high. I wouldn't be surprised to see them win by 30 or 40 points, but I don't think they are going to run up the score either. Maiava probably plays about a half in this game. I'm backing the under 50.5 for the USC team total. I like Miller to get 2+ touchdowns at +195 as a prop as well.

item.title: Death toll from mudslides, flooding at Nepal-China border climbs past 670, nearly 3,000 missing
item.description: Nepal's flood and mudslide death toll reaches more than 670 with nearly 3,000 missing as rain and fog halt search and rescue operations in the disaster zone.
item.content:encoded:
The death toll from the devastating floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border has risen to at least 676 people, as rescue operations stall amid poor weather.

After Nepali authorities updated their figures Saturday, the combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 676 dead and nearly 3,000 people missing, according to The Associated Press. Chinese authorities have reported seven deaths and more than 550 missing, while Nepal’s disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 669 with 2,426 people missing.

Experts believe Wednesday's mudslides and flash flooding across Nepal and China's Tibet region were caused by a large chunk of ice breaking off a glacier and falling into the Lhende Khola River. Rescue operations at the main disaster zone have been complicated by damaged roads and difficulty establishing communication, and look only to get more difficult, as intermittent rain is expected through the weekend.

"Search and rescue operations have been temporarily halted because it is raining, and the weather is foggy," Narendra Pariyar, a top official for Nepal's Rasuwa district, told Reuters.

MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF

While Nepalese authorities have stressed they don't need countries to send people to help with general search and rescue, they did request that China send tunnel experts as up to 100 people are still trapped in a mud-filled hydropower plant tunnel.

ARMY BLACK HAWKS AIRLIFT 200-PLUS STRANDED CAMPERS AS MISSOURI FLOODS TRIGGER MORE 350 RESCUES

"We have already made requests for such specialised services and technical assistance in areas where we don't have enough expertise and technical know-how," Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Reuters.

China dispatched five such workers from Tibet by helicopter to assist, according to the country's state-affiliated Xinhua news agency.

COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION

Dramatic video showed the rescue of one such person as authorities from Nepal worked to drag the man out of the mud deluge.

Though impending rainstorms are likely to make rescue operations more difficult, officials say a previous threat from a lake that had formed on the border between Nepal and Tibet has substantially subsided.

MASSIVE GARBAGE HEAP COLLAPSES ONTO HOMES, KILLING AT LEAST 30 AS RESCUERS SEARCH FOR SURVIVORS

The lake had been overflowing into the Lhende Khola River, risking further flooding, but that risk had gone down by Saturday, according to Chinese officials.

Nepal's finance minister Swarnim Wagle estimated the country will need over $4 billion to rebuild after the disaster.

"This is just an estimate. Loss and damage is being assessed," he told Reuters.

Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Tim McGraw takes hard fall onstage during concert
item.description: Tim McGraw took a tumble during his concert at Riverbend Music Center in Cincinnati while performing "I Like It, I Love It." The star joked about the fall on social media.
item.content:encoded:

MORGAN WALLEN SMASHES PIANO ON STAGE AFTER EQUIPMENT FAILS MID-PERFORMANCE DURING CONCERT

I didn't want to, but I didn't think it was going to get better."

item.title: Tech investor mocks Vance’s call to hire Americans as 'DEI', gets blasted by Trump officials in H-1B firestorm
item.description: Y Combinator investor Ankit Gupta mocked JD Vance's call to prioritize hiring Americans over H-1B visas, sparking backlash from the Trump administration.
item.content:encoded:
Ankit Gupta, a general partner at the influential Silicon Valley startup accelerator Y Combinator, drew criticism from Trump administration officials after mocking Vice President JD Vance’s call to prioritize American workers over hiring cheaper foreign labor.

The controversy began after the Trump administration proposed a $103,265 fee for many new H-1B visa petitions. As it stands, the H-1B visa program allows U.S. companies to hire foreign workers for specialty occupations and is overwhelmingly used by the tech industry. However, it has long been controversial among some conservatives, who say it is abused by tech companies to bring in cheap labor to replace American workers, many of them from India.

The proposed fee would make it costlier for American tech companies to rely on such labor and could give them an incentive to hire Americans instead, something Vance has emphasized repeatedly, such as when he recently declared, "If an American corporation needs workers, it should hire and train Americans."

Y Combinator general partner Ankit Gupta, who has since restricted his X posts from public access, mocked Vance, saying in purported screenshots, "In a win for the woke left DEI is back."

VANCE WARNS THERE WILL BE A 'SOCIALIST PRESIDENT IN THIS COUNTRY' IF GOP DOESN'T FIX ECONOMY FOR YOUNG PEOPLE

Gupta's comments comparing prioritizing American workers over foreign labor to DEI sparked a wave of criticism from several Trump administration officials and renewed a broader debate over H-1B visas, Silicon Valley hiring practices, and whether American workers—particularly younger and entry-level tech workers—are being disadvantaged by companies’ reliance on foreign-worker visa programs.

Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D’Esposito replied, "Ankit Gupta thinks hiring Americans first—in America—is ‘DEI.’ No, Ankit. It’s called putting your own citizens first. American companies. American jobs. American workers first. If that offends you, the problem isn’t America. It’s your sense of entitlement."

FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson criticized Gupta’s rhetoric as part of a larger phenomenon of contempt for American workers.

"I’m deeply uncomfortable with wealthy investors attacking American workers like this. I’m afraid it’s increasingly obvious to many people that individuals such as this guy do not have the best interests of America and her citizens in mind," he said. "The purpose of the American economy is to promote the general welfare of American workers, not provide jobs for the rest of the world."

In response to Ferguson's post, Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan wrote, "YC supports hiring and funding Americans."

Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon also weighed in, sharing a lengthy post criticizing what she described as abuses of the H-1B program and other foreign-worker programs.

"Our federal (and most state) employment laws mandate a level playing field for American workers vis-à-vis foreigners — yet many American tech (and other) companies prefer to hire cheaper/exploitable foreign workers to do routine jobs Americans could do, and they do this by failing to post jobs on their normal hiring channels (PERM violations), letting foreign-born hiring managers pipeline cheap foreign labor from body-shop mills over American workers (H1-B abuses), lie about their eligibility for no-cap H1-B hiring, abuse other visa categories such as J-1 visas (we see you, universities!), abuse OPT hiring to get cheap, exploitable foreign labor, and sometimes — getting super arrogant, gaslight laid-off and sidelined Americans while doing any of the above," she wrote.

CEO UNDER FIRE FOR MASS LAYOFFS AMID FOREIGN WORKER HIRING SPREE NOW APPOINTED TO FED'S TASK FORCE ON JOBS

Other commentators, ranging from policy think tanks to former Trump officials, spoke to Fox News Digital about the controversy.

John Miano, an attorney with the Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR), said the debate speaks to fundamental questions about the role of the United States and its immigration system.

"The center of this dispute is over what America is. I, and I think most Americans, believe America as a nation state; a commonwealth for the improvement of its citizens. Mr. Gupta clearly views America as an [economic] zone. The graves at Arlington and cemeteries around the world are not the product of Americans fighting and dying to save an economic zone. I would not want to share a foxhole with Mr. Gupta," he told Fox News Digital. 

He added, "There is no such thing as the [Libertarian] ideal of economics without borders. I would wager that Mr. Gupta opposes open borders regarding intellectual property. The H-1B program is designed to replace Americans with cheap foreign workers. The U.S. Congress is apparently the only national legislature that has voted to make it explicitly legal to replace citizens with foreign workers, as it has done with H-1B. The H-1B wage system is designed to allow employers to pay H-1B nonimmigrants extremely low wages. The biggest problem with H-1B is that it works exactly as Congress designed it to work."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Former Trump Appointee and Senior Advisor to the U.S. Senate, Mary Marslender, now a Republican consultant, explained how tech companies specifically find loopholes in the rules to avoid hiring Americans, particularly those trying to enter the job market.

"The uncomfortable reality is that many large American corporations prefer cheaper foreign labor because it gives them greater control over mid- to entry-level positions, all while telling Washington that qualified American workers can't be found. Immigration lawyers have been caught on video admitting their goal is to avoid hiring qualified Americans," she said. "Some have even confessed to placing job ads in obscure newspapers where Americans are unlikely to look, and then, if a qualified American applies, interviewing them specifically to find a legal basis to disqualify them. Prioritizing cheap foreign labor over American workers denies Americans jobs, particularly young people who need the firsthand job experience to launch their careers. American jobs should go to Americans first."

Theo Wold, a former acting assistant attorney general and former White House deputy assistant to the president for domestic policy under Trump, argued that part of what makes America great historically is its amazing pool of native talent.

"Jack St. Clair Kilby and Robert Noyce invented the microchip. They also both grew up in America's heartland. From airplanes and the television to nuclear submarines and the internet, American genius invented the modern world. But today's Silicon Valley elites would rather replace the next Robert Noyce with a foreign national on an H-1B visa than invest in American talent. America has a unique convergence of brainpower and risk tolerance. And our young people took the challenge and are excelling in STEM," he said. "America now graduates enough American STEM students to fill every opening in America’s tech and tech-related industries. We should be encouraging our young talent to build anew, rather than replace them with cheap labor widgets from Guangdong and Andhra Pradesh."

item.title: 'The Dog Stars' Review: Jacob Elordi fights for survival in Ridley Scott's dull post-apocalyptic western
item.description: Fox News Digital reviews 20th Century Studios' "The Dog Stars" starring Jacob Elordi, Josh Brolin, Margaret Qualley, Guy Pearce and Allison Janney. Directed by Ridley Scott.
item.content:encoded:
Ridley Scott has directed some of Hollywood's most iconic movies, from "Alien" and "Blade Runner" to "Thelma & Louise" and "Gladiator." But over the past decade, his films have mostly ranged from OK to meh. 

Unfortunately, his latest falls in the latter category. 

"The Dog Stars," adapted from Peter Heller's 2012 novel, follows Hig (Jacob Elordi), a mechanic trying to navigate a post-apocalyptic America that had been ravaged by a deadly flu years earlier. He has taken shelter at an abandoned Colorado airport and is joined by Bangley (Josh Brolin), a brutish former Marine with great aim, and Hig's Belgian shepherd, Jasper. 

‘MUTINY’ REVIEW: JASON STATHAM TAKES NO PRISONERS IN MINDLESS BUT AMUSING BRAWLER FLICK ON THE HIGH SEAS

The routine is as follows: Hig flies into Denver in his little yellow plane to seek supplies, stops by his old house, triggering flashbacks of his late wife, occasionally makes deliveries to a rural community of Mennonite farmers, and sometimes joins Bangley in killing trespassers who may be infected with the virus before burning their bodies as a precaution.

Hig thinks there is more civilization beyond the mountains, namely in Grand Junction. Bangley thinks it's a fool's errand and that leaving Eric would certainly lead to death. But Hig can't deny his own convictions, so he ultimately decides to seek life elsewhere. 

‘THE END OF OAK STREET’ REVIEW: ANNE HATHAWAY, EWAN MCGREGOR FIGHT DINOSAURS IN SURPRISINGLY FUN MOVIE

He'll come across some interesting characters on his journey, like the boorish rancher Jack and his daughter Cima (Guy Pearce and Margaret Qualley) and the eccentric Darlene (Allison Janney). There's also what's been dubbed the "Reapers," a group of tatted savages who will kill and destroy anything in their path. 

The cast does a fine job. Elordi, the Australian up-and-comer known for his breakout role in HBO's "Euphoria" and appearing more recently in "Wuthering Heights" and Netflix's "Frankenstein" (which earned him his first Oscar nomination), is flexing his leading man muscles. Both Brolin and Pearce earn a few laughs for their rough-around-the-edges performances. And Janney elevates any project she's in, regardless how zany her character is. 

'TONY' REVIEW: ANTHONY BOURDAIN'S COMING-OF-AGE STORY UNFOLDS IN CHARMING DRAMEDY

However, I never felt strongly invested as a viewer. Except for a few gun battles, "The Dog Stars" was fairly dull. Despite Elordi's best efforts, Hig is a run-of-the-mill dystopian protagonist, so there isn't much to work with (perhaps the source material is to blame). 

The guitar-forward score from Harry Gregson-Williams only furthers the film's sleepy western vibe. At least all the mountain scenery was pleasant to look at.

‘SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY’ REVIEW: TOM HOLLAND, ZENDAYA RETURN FOR ACTION-PACKED, EMOTIONAL SEQUEL

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Ridley Scott's "The Dog Stars" is the latest installment in the prolific director's middling stretch of films that will likely leave the mind shortly after viewing. And when that happens, you question why the movie was made to begin with.

"The Dog Stars" is rated R for strong violence and language. Running time: 1 hour, 58 minutes. In theaters now.

Hilaria Baldwin is taking the phrase "squeeze in a workout" to a whole new level.

The 42-year-old "Nation's Dumbest" contestant and mother of seven told Fox News Digital her fitness routine doesn’t always happen in a gym — or even in a dedicated workout space. Sometimes, it happens right there in the bathroom.

"I run every day… I found being a mom, if I can get 30 minutes of my cardio, it helps my mind... It gets me like sort of a little bit more regulated with my nervous system, so I really like that," she shared when asked about her go-to workout with a hectic schedule.

HILARIA BALDWIN SHARES MARRIAGE LESSON SHE TELLS FRIENDS AFTER SURVIVING 'UPS AND OUR DOWNS' WITH ALEC BALDWIN

"Then I obviously do my yoga, my little bathroom workouts, or just like a stop-and-drop little workout. I love Physique 57. Any kind of barre classes I think are really great."

Last month, she gave her fans a front-row look at exactly what those workouts can look like, showing off her physique in a bikini while demonstrating glute exercises in a bathroom.

HILARIA BALDWIN FLAUNTS FIT FIGURE IN BIKINI AS FANS MARVEL AT MOM OF 7

"Can’t touch his toes. I literally married the most inflexible person I have ever met."

'PERFECT' WORKOUT FORMULA CAN TAKE JUST 10 MINUTES A DAY, HILARIA BALDWIN SAYS

item.title: Stunned couple unearths 150-pound mystery hidden beneath their backyard for decades
item.description: A San Francisco couple unearthed a remarkable 150-pound limestone sculpture in their Russian Hill backyard, sparking a mystery with possible ties to artist Ralph Stackpole.
item.content:encoded:
A couple in San Francisco recently unearthed a 150-pound limestone sculpture buried in their backyard — setting off a search to uncover who created it and how it got there.

Greg Gatwood was doing yard work at the couple's Russian Hill home in May when he came across what he initially thought was a piece of concrete buried in the ground as his partner Judy Gittelsohn stood nearby.

Gatwood told Fox News Digital he tried to pry the object loose with a shovel before grabbing a pickaxe — and then spotted what appeared to be lips and a nose "peering" back at him.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MYSTERIOUS FACE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES IN BOOK OF REVELATION CITY

"I thought, well, maybe I should just break it into smaller pieces," Gatwood said. "Then I realized it was a statue.

"It was like something you see in a movie, almost cinematic, you know — a big beautiful statue like this."

Gittelsohn said she was stunned when Gatwood showed her the enormous, two-foot-wide statue — and was impressed by the quality of its craftsmanship.

"I was just shocked," she said. "What an enormous find."

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MASSIVE ARTIFACT DEPICTING PHARAOH THOUGHT TO HAVE CHALLENGED MOSES IN EXODUS

She added, "I was surprised. I was just gobsmacked."

Three months after their discovery, the couple is still searching for answers.

Gittelsohn, a professional artist, said she researched the sculpture. She believes it dates to the 1930s and may be connected to artists working under the Works Progress Administration (WPA).

The couple's home is near the former San Francisco Art Institute, where prominent sculptor Ralph Stackpole taught for decades — leading Gittelsohn to believe the piece may have a connection to him or one of his students.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

One clue supporting that theory, she said, is that the sculpture was carved from relatively inexpensive limestone rather than costlier materials such as marble or granite.

Gatwood believes the statue may have been used as garden art and that it was eventually buried with time.

"It's quite possible this statue was displayed in the garden and not so much buried, but just lost," he said.

After the couple received local attention for their find, Gittelsohn said a 93-year-old woman took an Uber to their home with her walker and knocked on their door.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The woman — one of several people who have reached out to the couple since the discovery became public — told them she had previously held a show featuring Ralph Stackpole's work. 

In September, the couple plans to put the sculpture on public display at the American Messenger Gallery in hopes that someone may recognize the piece or know who created it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"We think someone will eventually recognize it," Gatwood said.

The story comes about a year after a New Orleans couple made a similarly mysterious discovery in their backyard.

At the time, Daniella Santoro and Aaron Lorenz unearthed an ancient Roman funerary artifact that had been missing from an Italian museum for decades.

item.title: Kyle Busch's final words about Daytona come with a sobering Dale Earnhardt twist
item.description: The Coke Zero Sugar 400 marks the first NASCAR Cup Series race at Daytona International Speedway since Kyle Busch's stunning death back in May.
item.content:encoded:
It doesn't take long to spot a Kyle Busch fan at Daytona International Speedway.

In fact, drive under the tunnel and into the infield, and a "Rowdy Forever" banner is the first thing that greets you. It's not the only one. Not even close.

They're everywhere this weekend. Of course, that's expected.

This is the first NASCAR Cup Series race at Daytona since Busch's stunning death in May. The Coke Zero Sugar 400 is set to close the regular season later tonight — a little over three months since the sport lost its modern day Dale Earnhardt.

For better and for worse, those two will forever be attached at the hip.

KYLE BUSCH'S CHILLING MESSAGE AFTER FINAL NASCAR WIN A PAINFUL ENDING FOR MOURNING FANS

Busch's death in May was the first major NASCAR death for an active driver since Earnhardt died on the final turn of the 2001 Daytona 500.

For decades, Daytona gave Dale fits. He could win all the races, except the race.

Busch won just once at Daytona during his two decades in a Cup car, and never won a 500. It was the crown jewel he never got.

Lord knows he tried. Came close a couple times, too. Earlier this year, Busch grabbed his first Daytona 500 pole. He led 19 laps, but he fizzled late.

No, Kyle never loved Daytona the way Dale Earnhardt did. But he appreciated it. He respected it.

During February's 500, he led the third lap of the race, which was dedicated to Dale Earnhardt on what was the 25th anniversary of his death.

"Led lap 3 for Dale plus a few more today," he posted days after the race. "Made it to the end, just not in the right spot."

Now, the series returns for the first time since his death — and for the first time without an Earnhardt or a Busch in the field since 1978.

Yep. That's right. Saturday night's race will be the first Cup race at Daytona without an Earnhardt or a Busch in the field in 48 years. February 19, 1978.

For those who don't remember, Bobby Allison won that Daytona 500. Earnhardt would make his first Daytona start months later in the Firecracker 400.

Incredible. Forty-eight years. Nearly five decades!

So, yes, this sport has Earnhardt and Busch in its blood. Dale died in the '01 Daytona 500, which was Kurt Busch's first race. Kyle came into the series five years later as a rookie with Hendrick Motorsports.

UNEARTHED FAN VIDEO SHOWS WHO KYLE BUSCH REALLY WAS, NASCAR'S DARKEST HOUR & BUBBA WALLACE'S 'ROWDY' STORY

He'd go on to win 63 Cup races over the next two decades, including a pair of championships. He had 234 wins across all three NASCAR national series.

Busch won one Coca-Cola 600, two Southern 500s, and three Indianapolis 500 victories. He won once official race at Daytona, but did win a couple duels and the one Busch Clash on the road course back in 2021.

But Kyle never scored that elusive 500.

"Yeah, it’s a box we got to check," he said earlier this year. "Here we are. This is an opportunity to be able to do that. I’ve come down here a lot of years."

Daytona was never great to Kyle. It wasn't his favorite place to race. He didn't have the best luck.

But coming back here this weekend, it's clear this place misses him.

And like Dale, he's still everywhere you look.

item.title: AEW All In 2026 match card, preview and predictions
